take: Criquet makes golf shirts that never announce themselves as golf shirts, which is how the same four-button placket ends up on a Butler tee box and at a South Congress bar three hours later. Billy Nachman and Hobson Brown have known each other since kindergarten in Manhattan, where they grew up in prep-school polos and coat-and-tie dress codes, and they started the company in Austin in 2010. It begins in a closet, with the vintage golf shirt Nachman’s grandfather left behind: four buttons, a long placket, a collar that had opinions. They rebuilt it with a flap chest pocket, removable collar stays so the collar never bacons at the tip, and an organic-cotton pitch that was ahead of its time, and called it the Players Shirt. It runs in 100 per cent Peruvian pima today and still costs ninety-eight dollars.
story_extra: The name comes from the sound of crickets, by the brand’s own telling: the noise of being comfortably off-course. Criquet has never fully committed to being a golf brand. One half of the catalogue is Range Polos in brrr°, a mineral-infused yarn that moves heat off the skin, and Players Shirts you could tee off in at Butler. The other half runs pearl snaps, fine-wale corduroy in burnt orange and a loop-terry shirt called Midnight Toker, which belongs on a pool deck more than a first tee. The two halves hang in the same closet.

Criquet is an Austin company in a way that shows up in the product. The longtime clubhouse-headquarters on South First had a putting green, an outdoor bar and a Bill Murray mural. The collaboration list reads like a city directory: Zilker Belts from across the river, YETI from fifteen minutes up the road, the home team Austin FC under an official MLS license, and a Willie Nelson “Willie Forever” collection that has since been delisted. Discmania, the Finnish house that supplies most of disc golf, printed the brand’s mascot Carl onto a three-disc set. The store currently carries a belt strap in Save Muny colors and a tee with a Lions badge, which is more Lions Municipal product than some golf labels carry product at all.

The catalogue runs past a thousand SKUs and all of it radiates from that one shirt: six live collabs at $45 to $150, six core staples at $98 to $128, and an Early Fall drop that puts sleeves on the Players Shirt in four colorways.
